value:
THE 'SAME-REGISTER-BOTH-SIDES' CAPABILITY -- a proof mode for a use where OUR word and the TARGET word read the SAME register number yet the relation does not contain the pair -- HAS AN EMPTY PAYOFF SET. Its population is exactly TWO rows image-wide, and NEITHER is servable by such a capability: one is a genuine value difference that no sound relation may admit, and the other is not a member of the class at all. Building it would ship a rule that closes zero functions, which claim.LZ_copy-form-taxonomy-and-payoff-inversion.20260901.v1 already names as the failure mode to avoid. THIS IS THE PAYOFF INVERSION RECURRING FOR THE THIRD TIME: LZ found it for the `unconditional` arrow (4 sites, 0 closable), WF found it for the pure inverse arrow (2 sites, 1 function), and it recurs here at 2 sites and 0 functions. The pattern is now regular enough to state as procedure: CENSUS THE POPULATION AND CONFIRM EACH MEMBER INDIVIDUALLY BEFORE BUILDING ANY PROOF MODE, because the members of a signature-defined class are routinely artifacts or already served.

HOW THE POPULATION WAS ISOLATED. The degenerate refusal shape 'use of BN is not value-equal to BN' -- same bank, same register number on both sides -- is precisely what a same-register capability would have to discharge, and it is mechanically greppable out of the ledger's refusal column. Image-wide over 93 register-field-only paired functions it occurs exactly twice.

MEMBER 1, game/audio/mempool::pool_garbage_collect +0x30 -- A GENUINE VALUE DIFFERENCE, PERMANENTLY UNSERVABLE. Ours: +0x20 `lwz r5,4(r3)` loads the node, +0x28 `addi r0,r3,@l` puts the &lbl_8031EB00 ENTRIES BASE in r0, +0x30 `mr r31,r0` copies that base out. Retail: +0x20 `lwz r0,4(r3)` loads the NODE into r0, +0x28 `addi r29,r3,@l` parks the entries base in r29 instead, +0x30 `mr r3,r0` copies the node out. Both words read g0; the two g0s hold DIFFERENT VALUES. Admitting that pair would make the relation unsound -- the mode's whole invariant is '(bank,a,b) in R => our a and the target's b hold the same value here'. The refusal is correct and no capability may remove it. Confirmed invariant across the entire 120-permutation declaration-order space (see attempt.WF_pool-garbage-collect-rederived-pin-escape-not-retired.20260901.v1: the 22-word and 14-word bodies refuse at the same site with the same message).

MEMBER 2, game/world/tower::SumnerDoSpeech +0x220 -- NOT A MEMBER OF THE CLASS; A POSITIONAL-PAIRING ARTIFACT. At +0x220 the two words are BYTE-IDENTICAL (`add r27,r29,r0` on both sides); the refusal fires because a bisimulation is checked at every use, not only at differing words. The fact was killed upstream by what a positional read renders as two differences at +0x1fc/+0x200 -- ours `addi r29,r4,0` then `addi r30,r3,0`, retail the SAME TWO INSTRUCTIONS IN THE OPPOSITE ORDER -- with a second swapped `lis` pair at +0x1f0/+0x1f8. That is a PERMUTATION, not a renaming, and it is ALREADY MODELLED: the shipped rule carries an `instruction_permutation` stage whose recorded mechanism names the correct FIVE-atom region and order [2,1,0,4,3] (the `lfs f31` SDA load at +0x1f4 sits between the two `lis` atoms, so the adjacent pair a byte scan suggests is the wrong window). The function ships byte-exact with NO `unproven_recolor_audit` escape. Nothing is open here.

THE TRANSFERABLE WARNING, which is the same one the LZ census issued about `li`/copy pairs and is here confirmed for the recolor bank: A SCREEN THAT DOES NOT MODEL THE PERMUTATION STAGE WILL REPORT SWAPPED ADJACENT INSTRUCTIONS AS REGISTER DIFFERENCES, and will then attribute the resulting downstream bisimulation failure to a register-level cause at an offset far from the real one -- here 0x20 bytes downstream, at a word that does not differ at all. When a value-inequality refusal lands on a word that is IDENTICAL on both sides, suspect an upstream permutation before designing any new relation: dump the definitions of the named register in both streams and check for an equal-multiset reordering.
